evals.name: check-run-errors
evals.prompt: I just ran the ihc_lab utility — check OpenObserve and tell me if anything errored and why.
evals.expected_output: Connects to OpenObserve via ihcsettings.json telemetry config, queries the lowercase 'ihc' stream, finds the 'Telemetry logs endpoint rejected export: HTTP 400 ... data dropped silently' Error log from service IhcLab with timestamp and severity, correctly reports no error-status spans, and acknowledges the indexing delay.

assertions.text: Report shows it reached OpenObserve at localhost:5080 (org default) using the ihcsettings.json telemetry settings and queried the lowercase 'ihc' stream (not 'Ihc').
Report identifies the real error log about the telemetry logs endpoint rejecting export with HTTP 400 / data dropped silently.
Report gives concrete evidence for the finding: timestamp, service (IhcLab), and severity (Error).
Report does not fabricate error-status spans; if it mentions traces it correctly notes there are no error spans.
Report acknowledges OpenObserve's indexing delay or the look-back window as a caveat when reasoning about completeness.

evals.name: diagnose-slow-spans
evals.prompt: Are there any failing or slow spans in the traces? Diagnose the worst one.
evals.expected_output: Correctly reports there are no ERROR-status spans (all UNSET), identifies the slowest span(s) by duration with operation_name and duration, follows a trace_id to give context, and presents durations in sane units.

assertions.text: Report shows it reached OpenObserve and queried the 'ihc' traces stream using the ihcsettings.json config.
Report correctly states there are no ERROR-status spans (span_status is UNSET for all), rather than inventing failing spans.
Report identifies the slowest span(s) by duration, naming the operation_name and a duration value.
Report follows a trace_id to show the worst operation's context (e.g. its spans or parent/child relationship).
Durations are presented in sane, clearly-labelled units (microseconds converted to ms or explicitly labelled), not raw unexplained huge integers.

evals.name: silent-failure
evals.prompt: Something's silently failing at runtime — the app doesn't show an obvious error. Look at the telemetry and figure out what.
evals.expected_output: Searches both logs and traces, surfaces the 'data dropped silently' HTTP 400 telemetry-export error as the root cause with evidence (message, service, timestamp, any trace_id), and accounts for indexing delay.

assertions.text: Report shows both logs and traces were searched (not just one).
Report identifies the telemetry-export HTTP 400 'data dropped silently' error (or the actual error present) as the root cause of the silent failure.
Report backs the root cause with concrete evidence: message, service, and timestamp.
Report shows it used the ihcsettings.json telemetry config and the correct lowercase 'ihc' stream.
Report acknowledges OpenObserve's indexing delay or look-back window when reasoning about completeness.

evals.name: check-metric-reached-backend
evals.prompt: I added an ihc.edit.apply counter and an ihc.edit.apply.duration histogram and just ran OpenVisual. Did they actually reach OpenObserve, and what does the duration distribution look like?
evals.expected_output: Recognises that metrics are a separate signal from logs and traces, queries them with --metric (or --type metrics --sql), resolves the histogram to its _bucket/_count/_sum family rather than its bare name, scopes to the run with service_instance_id, and reads the _bucket rows as CUMULATIVE counts keyed by the le boundary.

assertions.text: Uses the metrics path (--metric, or --type metrics with --sql) rather than the default logs/traces error query, which cannot see metrics at all.
Refers to the histogram through its _bucket/_count/_sum family, and does not report the bare histogram name as an empty or missing stream.
Scopes the run with service_instance_id (the logs spelling) and not service_service_instance_id, which is the traces spelling and would match nothing.
Interprets _bucket values as cumulative counts per le boundary with a final le='inf' total, rather than as per-bucket counts.
If no points are found, reports it as unknown pending the indexing/export delay rather than concluding the instrument is not wired.
